docRequirement: llm-gateway-protocol.md:157 binds a gateway model-discovery request to a no-redirect transport: "The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential can't leak to a redirect target." The same line's second sentence states the intent — "A gateway that responds slowly or redirects `/v1/models`, even `http` to `https`, fails discovery silently; serve the endpoint directly at the configured base URL." So: a 3xx on the model-list endpoint must abort discovery, never be followed, and the credential header must reach only the configured base URL.
current: Both credentialed model-list fetches use a bare `fetch` with no `redirect` field, so the WHATWG default `"follow"` applies. (1) `fetchNestorModels` — packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/nestor.ts:41-43 is `await fetch(NESTOR_MODELS_URL, { headers: { 'Nestor-Token': credentials.apiKey ?? '' } })`, where `credentials.apiKey` is the dp gateway JWT and `NESTOR_MODELS_URL` is the hardcoded constant at nestor.ts:10. (2) `anthropicDriver.fetchModels` — packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.ts:50 is `await fetch(`${baseUrl}/v1/models?${params}`, { headers })`, with `headers['x-api-key'] = apiKey` at :33 (or `headers.authorization = Bearer …` at :35). The fetch spec strips only `Authorization`/`Cookie`/`Proxy-Authorization` across an origin change, so the custom headers `Nestor-Token` and `x-api-key` are replayed to a redirect target host verbatim. Nothing mitigates one layer up: the only global fetch wrapper, `installFetchTrustChain` at packages/shared/src/config/network-runtime.ts:236-265, fills in `proxy`/`tls` only and spreads `init` through unchanged (:249-253); `Response.redirected` is read nowhere in the repo (grep -a). Both paths are live: packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/index.ts:87-101 routes the built-in Nessy Gateway compat connection to `fetchNestorModels`, dispatched from `startAll`'s immediate non-blocking fetch at index.ts:190 and from `refreshNow` at index.ts:224 (connection created, auth completed, manual refresh); packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/registry.ts:23-29 reuses the same function for `providerType: 'codex-runtime'` on a 60-minute interval. Secondary, same two lines: neither request has any timeout. nestor.ts:41 has no `signal` at all, and although `timeoutMs` is threaded in (packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/anthropic.ts:13,26 → packages/shared/src/agent/backend/factory.ts:451), drivers/anthropic.ts:17 destructures only `{ connection, credentials }`, so the value is passed and ignored and no `AbortSignal` reaches :50. Sibling call sites are not affected: packages/shared/src/agent/diagnostics.ts:152-165 is an unauthenticated `HEAD` probe, and `testOpenAiCompatible` (drivers/pi.ts:269-273) and `listModelsViaHttp` (drivers/pi.ts:65-72) send `Authorization: Bearer`, which the fetch spec strips on a cross-origin redirect. The option is used deliberately elsewhere in-repo, so this is an omission and not a platform limit: packages/shared/src/auth/oauth.ts:237 sets `redirect: 'manual'` and packages/shared/src/plugins/plugin-manifest-probe.ts:146 sets `redirect: 'follow'` explicitly.
divergence: The URL, method and header values are all correct; the delta is one absent `RequestInit` field at each of two call sites. We follow redirects where the page requires a redirect to be a failure, so a 30x from the gateway (or from a TLS-terminating proxy in front of it) forwards the gateway JWT / API key to a third host instead of aborting discovery. This is not a key-name mismatch and not a response-parsing difference. Secondary delta from the same doc sentence: the documented 3-second request timeout has no counterpart — nestor.ts:41 has no timeout, and drivers/anthropic.ts ignores the `timeoutMs` it receives. Explicitly NOT a divergence: the rest of the documented request shape (`/v1/models`, `limit=1000`, the `data[]` envelope, the claude/anthropic id-prefix filter) does not transfer to the Nestor path — that endpoint is Nessy's own corporate REST route `/api/v1/cli/models` returning a bare `NestorModel[]` (nestor.ts:10,22-31,49), by design; only the no-redirect hardening transfers.

change.what: One line: add `redirect: 'error'` to the fetch init at :41-43, alongside the existing `headers`. `redirect: 'error'` makes fetch reject before the second request is issued, and the existing caller already treats a throw as failure (index.ts:97-101 logs `Nestor fetch failed` and keeps the stale persisted list), so no caller changes. Optional same-edit hardening for the doc's timeout half: add `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000)` — keep it a throw so the same catch path applies; do not swallow it into an empty model list, which would wipe the persisted catalog via index.ts:166-169.

One line: add `redirect: 'error'` to the fetch init at :50 (`{ headers, redirect: 'error' }`). While in the same function, resolve the dead timeout thread: either destructure `timeoutMs` at :17 and pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` on the same call, or drop `timeoutMs` from the driver contract — today it is supplied by both server-core fetchers and silently unused. Prefer wiring it; the existing throw at :51-53 already funnels failures to `_doRefresh`'s catch.

The first test already captures `init` per call (:49-51) and asserts on `url`/`token` (:73-76) — extend that recorded tuple with `redirect: init?.redirect` and assert `'error'`. Add one negative case: a stub that rejects (`throw new TypeError('unexpected redirect')`, the shape `redirect: 'error'` produces) and assert `fetchNestorModels` rejects rather than returning an empty model list.
The existing stub at :12 ignores `init`. Capture it and assert `init.redirect === 'error'` on the first page request. If `timeoutMs` gets wired, assert a `signal` is present too.

blastRadius: `fetchNestorModels` has exactly two callers: packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/index.ts:93 (built-in Nessy Gateway `pi_compat` connection, gated by `isNestorConnection`) and packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/registry.ts:26 (`CodexModelFetcher`, `refreshIntervalMs` 60 min, `providerType: 'codex-runtime'`). Entry points are `ModelRefreshService.startAll` (index.ts:177-206 — Nestor connections get the immediate fetch but no timer, index.ts:194) and `refreshNow` (index.ts:224), i.e. app startup, connection creation, dp-auth completion and the manual refresh button. `anthropicDriver.fetchModels` is reached only through `fetchBackendModels` (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/factory.ts:423-453) via packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/anthropic.ts:23; factory.ts:430-432 throws `CLAUDE_DISABLED_ERROR` unless `isProviderEnabled('claude')`, and `PROVIDER_FLAG_DEFAULTS.claude` is `false` (packages/shared/src/feature-flags.ts:129), so in a default build that half is unreachable. No wire, IPC or schema boundary is crossed — `redirect` is a per-request fetch option and the `ModelFetchResult` shape is untouched. There IS a persistence boundary downstream, but only on the success path: index.ts:166-169 `updateLlmConnection(slug, { models, defaultModel })` rewrites the stored connection catalog, and the failure path at index.ts:124-128 already preserves the stale list — which is why the fix must keep failure as a *throw* and never as an empty result. It does sit on the credential-egress boundary (the JWT read from `~/.nessy/dp_auth_creds.json`), the repo's auth risk trigger, so run the two focused test files plus `bun run typecheck:shared` and a server-core typecheck on the final diff. Tests touching these lines: packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/__tests__/nestor.test.ts (130 lines, stubs `globalThis.fetch` and already inspects `init`) and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.test.ts (48 lines, stubs `globalThis.fetch`). No imported-plugin path reads this.
userImpact: None observable. Today the Nessy Gateway answers `/api/v1/cli/models` directly, so the model picker fills normally and no user sees a difference either way. It surfaces the moment something in front of that path answers with a 3xx — a gateway misconfiguration, an ops-side path move, or a TLS-terminating corporate proxy that redirects to a login host: at startup and on every Nessy Gateway auth/refresh the app would silently hand the user's `Nestor-Token` JWT to whatever host the 30x names, with no dialog, no toast and no log line naming the new host (index.ts:96 logs only a model count). The user-visible symptom in that scenario is nothing at all, or at most a stale model list in Settings → AI; the leak is invisible. Making it surface takes only a 302 on that path — a redirect target logging its inbound headers is the whole demonstration.
notes: Every file and line cited above was read in this session (nestor.ts, drivers/anthropic.ts, drivers/pi.ts, diagnostics.ts, model-fetchers/index.ts, model-fetchers/registry.ts, model-fetchers/anthropic.ts, factory.ts, feature-flags.ts, network-runtime.ts, both test files). Two things rest on the challenger's measurement rather than a re-run here: that a cross-origin 302 forwards `Nestor-Token`/`x-api-key` while stripping `Authorization`/`Cookie` (measured on Node v24.4.1/undici and Bun 1.3.14), and that `redirect: 'error'` suppresses the second request entirely. Both are WHATWG-spec behaviour and I did not re-measure them; I also did not measure Electron main's `globalThis.fetch` specifically, though `redirect` is a standard `RequestInit` field honoured by undici and Bun alike, and the repo already relies on the field at auth/oauth.ts:237. `effort: S` covers the production change (two one-line edits); adding the four test assertions pushes the diff toward S/M but no new file is needed — both test files exist and already stub `globalThis.fetch`. The 3-second-timeout half of the doc sentence is reported as a secondary delta on purpose: the Nestor endpoint is not the documented Anthropic-Messages discovery route, so its request shape is Nessy's by design and only the no-redirect hardening is a genuine contract miss.
